content.prompt: An arithmetic sequence has first term $a$ and common difference $d$. Complete the following to find its $n$th term formula:

answer.worked:
Each new term adds one common difference $d$:
$$\begin{aligned}a_4&=a+3d\\a_5&=a+4d\\a_n&=a+(n-1)d\end{aligned}$$
The $n$th term is obtained by adding $d$ to the first term $n-1$ times.

answer.worked:
The monthly payments form an AP with $a=200$, $d=20$ and $S_n=3720$.

$$\begin{align*}S_n&=\frac{n}{2}[2a+(n-1)d]\\3720&=\frac{n}{2}[2(200)+(n-1)(20)]\\3720&=\frac{n}{2}(380+20n)\\3720&=n(190+10n)\\n^2+19n-372&=0\\(n-12)(n+31)&=0\\n&=12\quad(n>0).\end{align*}$$

She has been repaying for 12 months. For the last payment:

$$\begin{align*}a_n&=a+(n-1)d\\a_{12}&=200+11(20)\\a_{12}&=420.\end{align*}$$

Her last payment is $\$420$.

content.prompt:
In an arithmetic sequence, the fifth term is $9$ and the twenty-first term is $425$.
What is the smallest value of $n$ such that the sum of the first $n$ terms in the sequence is at least $10\,487$?

Let the first term be $a$ and the common difference be $d$.
$$\begin{align*}
a+4d&=9 \\
a+20d&=425 \\
16d&=416 \\
d&=26
\end{align*}$$
Substitute into $a+4d=9$.
$$\begin{align*}
a+4(26)&=9 \\
a&=-95
\end{align*}$$
The required condition is $S_n\geq 10\,487$.
$$\begin{align*}
S_n&=\frac{n}{2}\left[2a+(n-1)d\right] \\
&=\frac{n}{2}\left[2(-95)+(n-1)(26)\right] \\
&=\frac{n}{2}(26n-216) \\
&=13n^2-108n
\end{align*}$$
So:
$$\begin{align*}
13n^2-108n&\geq 10\,487 \\
13n^2-108n-10\,487&\geq0
\end{align*}$$
Solve the corresponding quadratic equation.
$$\begin{align*}
n&=\frac{108\pm\sqrt{108^2+4(13)(10\,487)}}{2(13)} \\
&=\frac{108\pm\sqrt{556\,988}}{26} \\
&\approx -24.55,\;32.86
\end{align*}$$
Since $n$ is a positive integer and the parabola opens upwards, the smallest possible value is $n=33$.
